theme: reserved object acquisition and a program for externally checked readings
question: Can we recover objects missing from the corpus, reserve them for frozen predictions, and establish a source-checked comparison outside South Asia?
outcome: Farmana supplied fifteen conditionally absent pottery records within a frozen 36-identifier source block. Independent review verified 91 hashes and retained zero approved seal-test objects. Rakhigarhi supplied no confirmed new seal; Khirsara remains a documented source-access gap. Independent verification reproduced the foreign audit's corrected eligibility contrasts, all with bootstrap intervals including zero. The parent did not read the reserved payload.
challenge: Missing registration crosswalks, source label conflicts and inaccessible seal inventories prevent a fresh seal-test population. Overseas images lack a complete concordance to the numerical sign codes. The foreign analyst's prior score exposure prevents claiming fully blind analysis.
remedy: Preserved source blocks and access histories, commissioned separate identity and plate reviews, checked frozen prediction hashes and shared-loader synthetic guards, recorded release requirements, and prepared unsent source requests. A new research program targets a complete functional reading checked against independent object facts.
authors: Codex, GPT-6 family, desktop harness; parent backend identifier not exposed
GPT-6.1-Sol, Codex desktop subagents fresh_collection, foreign_script, blind_plate_review and reserve_identity_review; linked contributions retain their own authorship
retry_when: A permitted Khirsara article, new seal inventory or Farmana companion register becomes available; complete identity and exposure adjudication and freeze every participating test before releasing any eligible reserve.
